decisions.reason: A standard catalogue format close to the core display business, it costs little to keep on offer and preserves an option on customer demand for adjustable quarter-pallet solutions.
The pegboard-back shelf display is a cheap variant of the established offer, and with no evidence of failure the low holding cost justifies keeping it open.
The quarter-pallet shelf display is a core, low-cost format that fits existing production, so there is no reason to abandon it.
The eighth-pallet display complements the standard pallet formats at minimal extra cost, so keeping the option open is sensible.
The wooden pallet departs more from the cardboard core and may tie up different materials, but it offers diversification value that is still uncertain and not clearly disproven, so it stays for now.
The media display targets a possibly shrinking physical-media segment, but it is cheap to keep within the existing format range, so it is retained while demand is observed.
